history.summary: Bharat Milap Temple stands on the parikrama path of Kamadgiri hill (Majhgawan, Satna district, MP) and marks the spot where Bharata met Lord Rama at Chitrakoot to persuade him to return to Ayodhya. According to the Ramayana and Ramcharitmanas accounts, Rama's refusal moved even the rocks — the temple preserves the lotus footprints of the brothers imprinted on stone. Bharata returned with Rama's paduka (sandals) instead, ruling Ayodhya in his name. Nearby are the Mandavi Mandir (in honour of Bharata's wife Mandavi) and Bharat Koop, the well into which Bharata poured the holy waters he had gathered for Rama's coronation. The temple has modest architecture with simple carvings and paintings of Ramayana scenes; it is counted among the most emotional pilgrimage spots in Chitrakoot.

town_description: Chitrakoot is an ancient pilgrimage town spread across the Madhya Pradesh–Uttar Pradesh border, sacred in the Ramayana as the place of Lord Rama's 11-plus years of exile. Its key sites — Kamadgiri, Ram Ghat on the Mandakini river, Hanuman Dhara and Gupt Godavari — draw lakhs of pilgrims, especially on Amavasya days. The MP-side town is Chitrakoot (Satna district), connected by road and rail, with an operational domestic airport at nearby Karwi.
